summary: This agent is a LangGraph-based support automation assistant running with root privileges, wielding arbitrary shell execution and write capabilities, and shipping data to external vendor endpoints.

readable_mtls_key.note: mtls key baked into image layer: ['GW_CLIENT_CERT']

coverage.note: Repository source was not reached, leaving tool capability envelopes and declared destinations blind.

identity.mitigation: Move the value behind a secret reference or mounted file so it is not readable from the process table, and rotate the exposed value for JIRA_API_TOKEN.
identity.reason: Observed credential_inventory includes a plaintext secret in the environment (JIRA_API_TOKEN) and the agent runs as the root user.

api_access.mitigation: Require human approval for the destructive tools in this grant (jira.issue.update, s3.object.put, shell.run), and deny by default any tool not on the approved list for this agent's catalogue entry.
api_access.reason: Observed tool_names includes shell.run and destructive updates with an absent approval_policy and root user execution.

data_reach.mitigation: Narrow the mount to the specific paths the agent reads, and mount read-only unless writes are part of the task, specifically removing the docker socket mount.
data_reach.reason: Observed mounts includes a read-write docker socket (/var/run/docker.sock) and a broad read-write data mount (/data/support-exports) accessed as root.

data_flow.mitigation: Record the proxy's upstream provider and retention posture in the approved catalogue for llm-gw.internal, so prompt destinations are established rather than assumed.
data_flow.reason: Observed destinations includes an unverified inference proxy over plaintext HTTP (llm-gw.internal) and external egress to files.vendor-x.com.

injection_exposure.mitigation: Separate the context that reads untrusted content from the context that holds destructive tools like shell.run and s3.object.put, so ingested text cannot reach a tool call directly.
injection_exposure.reason: Observed tool_names includes acting tools while processing support exports and Jira tickets containing potentially untrusted content.

text_signals.clamp: model said 3; floored at 4 -- agent-authored text cannot alone cause a refusal
text_signals.mitigation: Treat the claim as unevidenced and remove it from the skill description in audit-status; compliance status belongs in the approved catalogue, not in text the agent controls.
text_signals.reason: Observed skills_inventory contains self-attestation of compliance in the audit-status skill and describes unattended bulk operations over sensitive data.
